items.title: StepTerrain
items.text:
StepTerrain(x_start, step_height, step_length=1.0, num_steps=1, base_height=0.0)

Bases: Terrain

Piecewise flat terrain with a flight of steps along the x axis

Height is base_height for \(x < x_{start}\), then rises by step_height at x_start and every step_length after that, for num_steps steps in total

The terrain stays at the top step height afterwards; with the default of a single step, step_length has no effect

items.title: HeightmapTerrain
items.text:
HeightmapTerrain(heights, resolution, x0=0.0, y0=0.0)

Bases: Terrain

Smooth terrain interpolated from a uniform grid of heights heights(i, j) is the height at \((x_0 + i r, y_0 + j r)\), where \(r\) is the grid resolution

Heights are interpolated with a bicubic Catmull-Rom spline, which passes through every grid height and has continuous height and slope

The height second derivatives are piecewise continuous

Outside the grid, the terrain extends flat from its closest edge value

Replaces the grid of heights and its origin, keeping the resolution. The grid may change size. Models using this terrain see the new heights from their next evaluation, so this must not be called while a solver is using such a model.

items.title: solvers
items.text: Submodule containing classes related to the SSQP solvers.

items.title: SolverState
items.text:
Bases: Enum

The state of the solver. States:

  • Success: Convergence was achieved.
  • Loose Success: Solver stopped after loose success tolerance was reached.
  • Constraint Success: Solver stopped after constraints were satisfied (with relevant option enabled).
  • Primal Infeasible: A QP subproblem was detected as primal infeasible (ADMM only).
  • Max Iter Reached: Maximum number of iterations reached before convergence was achieved.
  • Time Limit Reached: Maximum solve time reached before convergence was achieved.
  • Ongoing: The solver is ongoing.

items.title: LineSearchMethod
items.text:
Bases: Enum

The line search method to use for the SSQP update step. Available line search methods:

  • Filter line search: Accepts an update if there is an improvement in any of the three criteria functions (norm, gap or violation)
  • Merit function line search: Uses a merit function that is a weighted sum of each of the three criteria functions and its gradient to determine the update step

items.title: QPSolverType
items.text:
Bases: Enum

The solver type to use to solve the QP at each step. Available solvers:

  • ADMM: The custom ADMM implementation.
  • HPIPM: The HPIPM interior point solver, using the HPIPM library.
  • PIQP: The PIQP proximal interior point solver, using the PIQP library.

items.title: HPIPMMode

The HPIPM solver mode. Available modes:

  • Robust
  • Speed
  • Balance

items.title: ssqp
items.text:
Defines an SSQP problem solver based on a given SSQP model and the desired parameters.

SSQP is a Structure-exploiting Sequential Quadratic Programming solver. The solver starts with an initial guess (either provided, or zero) for the states (x) and controls (u) of an optimization problem over a time horizon H.

At each step, SSQP constructs a Quadratic Program at the current SSQP guess with a quadratic cost function and linearized constraints. This is done using the SSQP model, a model of the system being optimized which provides the necessary methods to linearize at each guess, like gradients and hessians.

The solver then utilizes a QP solver to produce a solution to the constructed QP, which can act as an update step for the current SSQP guess. Based on this solution, a line search method is used to update the current guess.

Termination criteria are then checked for the new SSQP guess. The process is repeated until convergence is reached.

items.title: feedbackGain
items.text:
feedbackGain(stage)

Feedback gain K (nu-by-nx) of the last QP at the given stage, giving the change du = K dx of the stage's controls for a change dx of its state. dx is in the tangent space of the dynamics, as returned by state_right_minus.

HPIPM returns the Riccati gain of its last interior point iteration. ADMM returns the gain of its final LQR, which also penalizes inactive constraints, so it is stiffer.

items.title: MPC
items.text:
MPC(model, ssqp_params=..., *, sqp_iters=5, qp_iters=50, max_time=-1.0, keep_convergence_data=False)

Helper class which utilizes SSQP to perform MPC for real-time SSQP-based control.

Repeatedly uses SSQP with low iterations to solve a problem for the current state of a system, applies the first of the generated controls, updates the initial guess using feedback from the system and a warm start using the previous solution and repeats the process.

Initialize an MPC helper for the given model, the given MPC, SSQP and QP parameters. Note that the max iterations used for SSQP and the QP solver, and the SSQP time limit (max_time, in seconds), will be determined by the MPC parameters only.

items.title: feedbackGain
items.text:
feedbackGain(stage)

Feedback gain K (nu-by-nx) of the last step at the given stage, giving the change du = K dx of the stage's controls for a change dx of its state. dx is in the tangent space of the dynamics, as returned by state_right_minus. Between steps, it corrects the first stage's controls for the measured state: u = u.stage(0) + K @ dynamics.state_right_minus(state, x.stage(0))

HPIPM returns the Riccati gain of its last interior point iteration. ADMM returns the gain of its final LQR, which also penalizes inactive constraints, so it is stiffer. PIQP does not provide a feedback gain.
